items.name: 350 Central Mass priorities
items.description: All-volunteer 350 Mass affiliate working on ending fossil fuel dependence, electrifying everything and environmental justice in Central Massachusetts, including support for the Fix the Grid campaign.

items.name: Join 350 Central Mass
items.description: Join the volunteer group; meetings are held on Zoom and all are welcome. Contact the group through its website for the link.

groups.name: Charles River Watershed Association
groups.description: Nonprofit founded in 1965 that uses science, advocacy and the law to protect and restore the Charles River, including work on stormwater and climate resilience across the watershed.

items.name: Cut the Crap: Sewage-Free Charles Campaign
items.description: CRWA campaign urging regulators to reject the draft Combined Sewer Overflow Long-Term Control Plan and pursue a sewage-free Charles River. Public comment is open through October 30 and includes public hearings.

items.name: Meet Your Watershed Event Series
items.description: CRWA event series introducing people to places across the Charles River watershed through walks, paddles, and other outings. No upcoming dates are currently listed.

items.name: Combined Sewer Overflow Control Plan Public Hearing #3
items.location: Somerville City Hall, Council Chambers, 93 Highland Ave, Somerville
items.description: Public hearing to comment for a sewage-free Charles.

items.name: Clean Charles Convening
items.location: Cabral Center, Northeastern University, 40 Leon St, Boston
items.description: Inaugural convening on making the Charles River swimmable: scientists, resource managers and advocates discuss what it would take to go from one or two swim events a year to beaches on the Lower Charles. All day at Northeastern's Cabral Center; registration required.

items.name: Run of the Charles Paddle Race
items.location: Charles River, Boston/Cambridge area (Herter Park finish)
items.description: Boston's annual paddle race since 1983, hosted by Charles River Watershed Association with Paddle Boston on the last Sunday of April. Kayaks, canoes and paddleboards choose a 3-, 6-, 9- or 14-mile relay course, then the Finish Line RiverFest (food trucks, live music). All skill levels; register as an individual or group.

items.name: Become a Volunteer Monthly Monitor
items.description: Apply to sample E. coli and record river conditions at a Charles River site at 6 AM each month; open sites include the New Charles River Dam, Medfield, and Bellingham. One-year commitment requested.

items.name: Volunteer for Invasive Plant Removals
items.description: Join CRWA volunteer events removing invasive plants such as bittersweet and water chestnut along the Charles River; group events are also available. Registration is first-come, first-served.

items.name: Become a Cyanobacteria Visual Monitor
items.description: Photograph and report possible cyanobacteria blooms along the Charles River using CRWA's submission form; observations feed EPA's BloomWatch program.

items.name: Volunteer as a Biological Monitor
items.description: Help assess the health of Charles River tributaries and streams by sampling aquatic life with CRWA.

items.name: Volunteer Photographer for CRWA
items.description: Join CRWA's community of volunteer photographers documenting nature, wildlife, and people enjoying the Charles River.

items.name: Submit a Public Comment on the CSO Plan
items.description: Urge regulators to reject the draft plan that would continue sewage discharges into the Charles River, by submitting public comment before the deadline.

groups.name: Green Energy Consumers Alliance
groups.description: Cambridge-based consumer nonprofit that educates and organizes households to switch to clean energy through programs for green power, electric vehicles, solar, heat pumps and efficiency, and advocates for climate policy.

items.name: Shave the Peak
items.description: Program that sends text or email alerts on peak electricity demand days so households can cut use, and supports advocacy for a cleaner grid.

items.name: Heat pump program
items.description: Advice, installer referrals and rebate information to help households install heat pumps.

items.name: Green Powered, Solar and Drive Green programs
items.description: Consumer programs for renewable electricity, solar options and electric vehicle adoption in Massachusetts and Rhode Island.

items.name: Shave the Peak: Save Energy When It Matters Most (webinar)
items.description: Webinar on what peak electricity demand is, how it affects affordability, and what households can do to reduce it.

items.name: Everything You Need to Know About Charging Adaptors
items.description: Webinar on EV charging adaptors.

items.name: Harvest Your Energy Festival (Medford)
items.location: Riverbend Park, Freedom Way, Medford, MA
items.description: Green Energy Consumers Alliance participates in the City of Medford festival with exhibits, art, food, live music and wind turbine tours.

items.name: Heat Pumps & Time-Varying Rates
items.description: Overview of heat pump rates in MA with DOER.

items.name: Emerging Clean Energy Technologies
items.description: One-hour webinar on emerging clean energy technology for households (smart thermostats, window heat pumps, portable batteries, plug-in solar): how it works and how it can lower bills and support a cleaner grid. RSVP online.

items.name: How to Use Online Tools to Plan an Electric Road Trip
items.description: Half-hour webinar on planning an electric-vehicle road trip, with demos of PlugShare and A Better Route Planner and time for questions. RSVP online.

items.name: Annual Fall Meeting
items.location: Artists for Humanity, 100 West 2nd St, Boston, MA
items.description: Green Energy Consumers Alliance's annual Fall Meeting at Artists for Humanity in Boston: an evening of networking and clean energy conversation. Tickets on sale; more details to come.

items.name: Winter Driving in an Electric Car
items.description: One-hour webinar on how cold weather affects electric vehicles, with tips for driving electric through a New England winter and time for Q&A. RSVP online.

items.name: Electric Vehicle Battery Health
items.description: Half-hour webinar on long-term EV battery health: the latest science, what affects a battery's life, and how to check a particular EV's battery. Q&A included; RSVP online.

items.name: Become an EV Ambassador
items.description: Sign up to be contacted about EV showcase events where you can bring your electric car and share your experience with prospective buyers.

items.name: Sign up for Shave the Peak alerts
items.description: Sign up for text or email alerts on peak electricity demand days with tips to reduce use.

groups.name: Climate Action Now Western Massachusetts
groups.description: Grassroots volunteer group in Western Massachusetts focused on climate justice organizing and public education; its youth wing is Youth Climate Action Now.

items.name: CREATE farmer mutual aid
items.description: Cultivating Relationships: Education | Action | Tending Earth. Volunteers join local farmers for work shifts through the season; sign-up form required.

items.name: Miyawaki mini-forest group
items.description: Climate Action Now's working group on Miyawaki-method mini-forests and local biodiversity.

items.name: No Clearcut for Profit (Eversource tree clearing)
items.description: Campaign led by Western Mass Towns for a Responsible Grid, promoted by Climate Action Now: a petition asking the Governor to limit Eversource's tree clearing across 11 towns, ahead of Eversource's Final Environmental Impact Statement (around December).

items.name: A Climate Justice Plan for Springfield
Fall Gathering: Nurturing biodiversity in a time of ecological chaos
items.description: Potluck and connection at 5:30 pm; interactive program 6–7:30 pm with Owen Wormser and Matt Verson, hosted by the Miyawaki Forest Group. RSVP appreciated.

items.name: Sierra Club Forest Protection Team Monthly Meeting
items.description: Monthly meeting of the Sierra Club Massachusetts Forest Protection Team, second Thursday 7–8:30 pm on Zoom. The Zoom link is on the event page.
items.recurrence: Second Thursday of each month, 7:00-8:30 PM

items.name: Racism, White Supremacy and Climate Justice Working Group Meeting
items.description: Monthly meeting of Climate Action Now's Racism, White Supremacy and Climate Justice working group, on Zoom. Email the organizer listed on the event page for the link.
items.recurrence: Second Monday of each month, 6:00-7:30 PM

items.name: Wildlands Campaign Working Group Meeting
items.description: Monthly meeting of the Wildlands Campaign working group (forest protection and natural climate solutions), 7–8:30 pm. Register through the link on the event page.
items.recurrence: Second Wednesday of each month, 7:00-8:30 PM

items.name: Monthly Gathering - 4th Monday
items.description: Climate Action Now's monthly gathering, fourth Monday 7–8:30 pm on Zoom. The registration link and details come in the newsletter.
items.recurrence: Fourth Monday of each month, 7:00-8:30 PM

items.name: MA Pollinator Network monthly session
items.description: Monthly MA Pollinator Network session: an expert talk on pollinators and how to support them, last Tuesday 7–8 pm on Zoom. Open to everyone, from home gardeners to researchers; talks are recorded for YouTube. Register for the link.
items.recurrence: Last Tuesday of each month, 7:00-8:00 PM

groups.name: Massachusetts Senior Action Council
groups.description: Statewide, senior-led grassroots group founded in 1981 that organizes older adults on health care, economic security, housing, transportation and racial justice.

items.name: Boston Chapter Meeting, Massachusetts Senior Action Council
items.location: Charles St. AME Church, 551 Warren St, Roxbury
items.description: Monthly in-person chapter meeting (most have a Zoom option) to discuss local and statewide issues and outreach. All are welcome.
items.recurrence: Second Thursday of each month, 12:30-2:30 PM

items.name: North Shore Chapter Meeting, Massachusetts Senior Action Council
items.description: Monthly in-person chapter meeting (most have a Zoom option) to discuss local and statewide issues and outreach. All are welcome.
items.recurrence: Third Wednesday of each month, 10:00-11:30 AM

items.name: Cambridge/Somerville Chapter Meeting, Massachusetts Senior Action Council
items.location: Central Sq. Senior Center, 806 Mass Ave, Cambridge
items.description: Monthly in-person chapter meeting (most have a Zoom option) to discuss local and statewide issues and outreach. All are welcome.
items.recurrence: Fourth Monday of each month, 11:00 AM-12:30 PM

items.name: Greater Springfield Chapter Meeting, Massachusetts Senior Action Council
items.location: Greater Springfield (contact the office for location)
items.description: Monthly in-person chapter meeting (most have a Zoom option) to discuss local and statewide issues and outreach. All are welcome.
items.recurrence: Fourth Wednesday of each month, 1:00 PM

items.name: Metro-North Chapter Meeting, Massachusetts Senior Action Council
items.description: Monthly in-person chapter meeting (most have a Zoom option) to discuss local and statewide issues and outreach. All are welcome.
items.recurrence: Fourth Wednesday of each month, 1:00-2:30 PM

groups.name: Neighbor to Neighbor Massachusetts
groups.description: Statewide organizing group that advocates on economic, racial and environmental justice, with a climate justice field program and environmental justice campaigns.

items.name: Dwight Street Garden
items.description: Neighborhood garden in Holyoke started by Neighbor to Neighbor on a vacant lot, producing food, sharing it and hosting organizing meetings.

items.name: Housing for All campaign
items.description: Statewide Neighbor to Neighbor campaign for affordable, stable housing and rent regulation.

items.name: Letter campaign: support the Clean Slate Act
items.description: Send a letter asking legislators to support the Clean Slate Act to automatically seal old criminal records.

items.name: Become a Neighbor to Neighbor member
items.description: Join Neighbor to Neighbor as a member in Holyoke, Lynn, Springfield, Worcester or statewide.

items.name: Sign up to be a LUCE verifier
items.description: Interest form to become a verifier in the community rapid-response network to protect neighbors from ICE.

groups.name: Tree Boston
groups.description: Dorchester-based nonprofit (formerly Speak for the Trees) that plants and cares for trees and advocates for tree equity in Boston neighborhoods, including a teen urban tree corps.

items.name: NeighborWoods Tree Plantings
items.description: Free shade trees planted at homes and businesses in Dorchester, Hyde Park, Roxbury and Mattapan each spring and fall; residents apply online.

items.name: Boston Tree Giveaways
items.description: Two or three free tree giveaway events each spring and fall for Boston residents.

items.name: Teen Urban Tree Corps
items.description: Paid summer and school-year program for Boston teens ages 14-18 covering tree care, field trips and green career exposure.

items.name: Tree Planting at Malcolm X Park - Roxbury
items.description: Volunteer tree planting event.

items.name: Annual Fall Benefit: Branching Out 2026
items.location: Southline Boston, 135 Morrissey Blvd, Dorchester, MA
items.description: Food, drink and tree-themed activities to support Tree Equity in Boston.

items.name: Tree Giveaway at The Urban Farming Institute
items.location: Urban Farming Institute, 487 Norfolk St, Mattapan, MA
items.description: Free tree giveaway.

items.name: Climb for the Canopy
items.location: Harvard Stadium, 79 N Harvard St, Allston, MA
items.description: Stadium-climb fundraiser; Tree Boston is first nonprofit partner for the Reach Green Stadium Challenge.

items.name: Free Tree Giveaway - Hyde Park Public Library
items.location: Hyde Park Branch, Boston Public Library, 35 Harvard Ave, Hyde Park, MA
items.description: Free tree giveaway.

items.name: Volunteer with Tree Boston
items.description: Sign up to water and mulch street trees, collect tree data, engage tree recipients, or help with outreach and events.

items.name: ICE Out For Good
items.description: Sunrise Movement national campaign encouraging people to press hotels, rental car agencies and restaurants not to serve ICE operations in their cities.

items.name: Green New Deal for Communities
items.description: Sunrise Movement national campaign pushing cities and towns to adopt local Green New Deal policies on housing, transit and public power.

items.name: Climate Standout in Beverly, MA
items.location: Odell Veterans Memorial Park, 56-98 Broadway, Beverly, MA
items.description: Volunteer-hosted climate standout at Odell Veterans Memorial Park, listed on the Sunrise Movement events feed.

groups.name: Boston Latin School Youth Climate Action Network
groups.description: After-school climate club at Boston Latin School that runs a youth climate summit, campaigns for sustainability education in grades 7-12 and coordinates a network of youth climate groups at other Massachusetts schools.

items.name: Annual BLS Trash Dash
items.description: Annual October student team competition to collect trash and recyclables on the Boston Latin School campus and Longwood area.

items.name: Annual Climate & Sustainability Youth Summit
items.description: Yearly free statewide student climate summit hosted by BLS YouthCAN.

items.name: Education for Sustainability campaign
items.description: BLS YouthCAN statewide campaign to incorporate sustainability lessons across subjects in grades 7-12.
